ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a transition-state structure: on the left is a four-membered carbon ring, the right side of the ring is connected to a section of carbon chain, the carbon chain is further connected to a nitrogen marked with a positive charge, below there is another nitrogen and it is represented in the form N=N; in the upper right there is a water molecule H–O–H; there are also curved arrows in the figure. Reasoning: According to the requirement, only bonds involving non-hydrogen are counted, and arrows are ignored. The four-membered carbon ring has 4 C–C bonds; there is 1 C–C bond between the ring and the side-chain carbon; there is 1 bond between the side-chain carbon and the adjacent N; the N=N double bond is counted as 1 heavy-atom bond. The O–H bonds of the water molecule involve hydrogen and are excluded. The total is 4 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 7.

method.method_draft: Inspect the drawing and tally only non-H bonds by substructure: the cyclobutane ring contributes 4 C–C bonds; the bond from the ring to the side-chain carbon contributes 1; the side-chain carbon to the adjacent N contributes 1; the N=N double bond contributes 1 heavy-atom bond. Ignore the O–H bonds in water and all curved arrows. Add 4 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 7.
